cases.note: Issue #1840. Each child's stat asks the index about that one name, not the whole listing, so ls of a large folder is linear: ls -l stats every child, a name the listing leaves out is a miss, and a write after the listing is found. Pinned against GNU coreutils in debian:stable-slim.
cases.command: mkdir -p /data/lsbig && for i in $(seq 100 219); do printf x > /data/lsbig/f$i; done; ls /data/lsbig | wc -l; ls -l /data/lsbig | grep -c '^-'; ls /data/lsbig/f150 /data/lsbig/f220; echo "rc=$?"; printf y > /data/lsbig/g; ls /data/lsbig/g; ls /data/lsbig | wc -l; rm -r /data/lsbig

expect.stderr: ls: cannot access '/data/lsbig/f220': No such file or directory
